subject: Economics
examFormat: Two papers forming a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1 has fifty multiple-choice questions in 1 hour for 50 marks. Paper 2 has eight essay-type questions in Sections A and B (Section A has two data response questions); candidates answer four questions in all, one from Section A and any three from Section B, in 2 hours for 80 marks.

topics.name: Definition and Scope of Economics
objectives: Explain scarcity and choice, scale of preference and opportunity cost
Explain the production possibility curve
Describe economic activities: production, distribution and consumption
Classify economic activities into primary, secondary and tertiary
topics.content: Scarcity and choice, scale of preference, opportunity cost, production possibility curve. Economic activities: production, distribution and consumption. Classification of economic activities as primary, secondary and tertiary and their relative contributions in terms of output/income, employment, savings, investment and foreign exchange.

topics.name: Factors of Production
objectives: Explain the meaning, characteristics and importance of land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship
topics.content: Land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship: meaning, characteristics and importance.

topics.name: Types and Basic Features of Economic Systems
objectives: Identify the types of economic system: capitalism, socialism and mixed economy
State the basic features of each
State the advantages and disadvantages of each
Explain the economic problems of society and the approaches for solving them under each system

topics.name: Basic Tools of Economic Analysis
objectives: Use tables, graphs and charts
Calculate and apply the arithmetic mean, median and mode
topics.content: Tables, graphs and charts. Some basic statistical measures and representations: arithmetic mean, median, mode and their simple applications.

topics.name: Demand
objectives: Explain the concept and law of demand, demand schedules and curves
Explain the reasons for exceptional demand curves
Identify types of demand: derived, composite, joint and competitive
Identify factors determining demand: price of the commodity, prices of other commodities, income, tastes, price expectation, etc.
Distinguish a shift of a demand curve from a movement along it
Explain the concept of elasticity of demand and its types (price, income and cross elasticities) and their measurement
Explain the importance of elasticity of demand to consumers, producers and government

topics.name: Supply
objectives: Explain the concept and law of supply, supply schedules and curves
Identify types of supply: composite, complementary and competitive
Identify factors determining supply: input prices, technology, prices of other commodities, climatic factors, etc.
Distinguish a shift of a supply curve from a movement along it
Explain the concept and measurement of elasticity of supply and its importance to producers and government

topics.name: Theory of Consumer Behaviour
objectives: Explain total, average and marginal utility and calculate utility schedules
Explain the law of diminishing marginal utility and the relationship between total, average and marginal utility
Explain the concept of consumer equilibrium and how it is determined
Explain the effects of changes in price on consumer equilibrium
Explain the relationship between marginal utility and the demand curve

topics.name: Theory of Price Determination
objectives: Explain the concept of the market and the interaction between demand and supply
Explain price determination under free and regulated markets
Determine equilibrium price and quantity in product and factor markets
Explain the effects of changes in supply and demand on equilibrium prices and quantities
Determine equilibrium price and quantity algebraically (introduction)
Explain price controls: maximum and minimum price regulations, their meaning and effects
Explain rationing and the black (parallel) market

topics.name: Theory of Production
objectives: Explain division of labour and specialization
Explain the scale of production (internal and external economies)
Explain total, average and marginal productivity and the law of variable proportions

topics.name: Theory of Cost and Revenue
objectives: Explain cost concepts: total, average, marginal, variable and fixed cost; short run and long run costs
Distinguish the economist's view of cost from the accountant's (opportunity cost and money cost)
Explain revenue concepts: total, average and marginal revenue, and marginal revenue product

topics.name: Market Structures
objectives: Describe the characteristics of the various market structures
Explain price and output determination under perfect competition and imperfect competition (monopoly and monopolistic competition)
Review cost and revenue concepts
Explain price discrimination

topics.name: Business Organizations
objectives: Describe the types and basic features of business enterprises: sole proprietorship, partnership, joint-stock companies (private and public), co-operatives, statutory corporations and joint ventures
Identify sources of funds
Explain the general and basic problems of business enterprises
Explain privatization and commercialization as solutions to problems of public enterprises
Explain indigenization and nationalization policies

topics.name: Distributive Trade
objectives: Describe the process of distribution
Explain the role of producers, wholesalers, retailers and co-operatives
Explain the role of government agencies in product distribution
Identify the problems of distribution and their solutions

subtopics.name: Population
objectives: Explain the determination and implication of the size and growth of population
Explain rural-urban migration
Explain the Malthusian theory of population
Describe geographical, age, sex and occupational distribution
Explain the importance and problems of census
Explain population and economic development (under-population, optimum population and over-population)

subtopics.name: Labour Market
objectives: Explain the concept of labour force and human capital, efficiency and mobility of labour
Explain factors affecting the size of the labour force, particularly population characteristics (age, sex, occupation, education, etc.)
Explain supply of and demand for labour and wage determination
Explain unemployment and underemployment
Explain the role of trade unions, employers' associations and government policies on labour and wages

topics.name: Agriculture
objectives: Describe the structure of agriculture (food crops, export crops, livestock, fisheries)
Describe systems of agriculture: peasant, commercial, co-operative and state farming
Explain the importance of agriculture to the national economy
Explain the marketing of agricultural products (commodity boards)
Explain agricultural policies (minimum agricultural prices)
Identify problems of agriculture and their remedies

topics.name: Industrialization
objectives: Explain the meaning and types of industry
Define the industrial concepts of plant, firm, industry and industrial estates
Explain the location of industry and localization
Explain the role of industrialization in economic development
Describe strategies of industrialization and its problems
Explain the link between agricultural and industrial development

topics.name: National Income
objectives: Explain national income concepts: Gross Domestic Product, Gross National Product, Net National Product, etc.
Describe the different ways of measuring national income and their problems
Explain the uses and limitations of national income data
Describe trends and structure of national income

subtopics.name: Money
objectives: Define money and describe its historical development, including barter and its problems
Describe the types, characteristics and functions of money
Explain the supply of and demand for money, the value of money and the price level

subtopics.name: Inflation
objectives: Explain the meaning, types, causes, effects and control of inflation

topics.name: Financial Institutions
objectives: Describe the types of financial institution: traditional, Central Bank, commercial bank, development bank, merchant bank, insurance companies and building societies
Explain the development and functions of financial institutions
Explain the meaning, types and functions of money and capital markets

topics.name: Public Finance
objectives: Explain fiscal policy and the objectives of public finance
Identify sources of government revenue
Explain taxation: types (direct and indirect), objectives, merits, demerits and incidence
Explain the principles/canons of taxation
Explain rates of taxation: proportional, progressive and regressive
Explain the composition/structure of public expenditure (recurrent and capital) and its effects
Explain the government budget and the national debt

topics.name: Economic Development and Planning
objectives: Explain the meaning of economic development and distinguish economic growth from development
Describe the characteristics and problems of developing countries
Explain the elements of development planning (objectives and problems of planning)
Identify types of plans: short term, medium term, perspective or long term, rolling plan, etc.

topics.name: International Trade and Balance of Payments

subtopics.name: International Trade
objectives: Distinguish domestic from international trade
Explain the basis of international trade, absolute and comparative cost advantage
Define and measure the terms of trade
Explain commercial policy objectives and instruments: tariffs (types) and direct control
Describe the trend and structure of West African countries' external trade

subtopics.name: Balance of Payments
objectives: Explain the role of money in international transactions
Explain the meaning and components of balance of payments and balance of payments disequilibrium
Explain balance of payments adjustments (exchange rate policy, exchange control, monetary and fiscal policies) and financing (use of reserves and international borrowing)

topics.name: Economic Integration
objectives: Explain the objectives, levels and features of economic integration
Explain the development and problems of economic integration in West Africa (ECOWAS)

topics.name: International Economic Organizations
objectives: Explain the development and role of OPEC, ECA, IMF, IBRD, AfDB, UNCTAD, etc.
Explain the relevance of such organizations to West African countries
topics.content: Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC); Economic Commission for Africa (ECA); International Monetary Fund (IMF); International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD); African Development Bank (AfDB); United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), etc.

topics.name: Major Natural Resources
objectives: Explain the development of major natural resources (petroleum, gold, diamond, timber, groundnut, etc.)
Explain their positive and negative effects on West African economies
